slides.title: The bottleneck is no longer access to AI — it is orchestration across real work
slides.body: Teams already have multiple AI tools. The operational gap appears when those tools must coordinate with people, data, approvals, and existing systems.
slides.proof: Design the workflow first. Choose models and agents as interchangeable execution components.
slides.footMessage: Build a shared view of the challenge before selecting interventions.

slides.title: A useful AI demo should make value visible at three operating levels

metrics.label: 01 · TIME
metrics.note: Reduce handoffs and repeated manual steps.

metrics.label: 02 · QUALITY
metrics.note: Make rules, evidence, and review points explicit.

metrics.label: 03 · SCALE
metrics.note: Turn one-off prompting into a repeatable workflow.

slides.footMessage: Assess success across the delivery model, not just implementation speed.

slides.title: Korn Ferry connects people, AI agents, business systems, and evidence in one flow
slides.footMessage: Define the roles, decisions and controls needed to make change sustainable.

slides.title: The demo should show the workflow moving from request to reviewed output
slides.footMessage: Make the decision path and evidence visible.

slides.title: The same system can support demos, pilots, and production without changing the visual grammar
slides.footMessage: Choose a phased approach before committing to scale.

slides.title: Start from the business workflow, then add AI only where it improves the operating model

steps.title: Map
steps.body: Define the current workflow and decision points.

steps.title: Measure
steps.body: Track time, quality, adoption, and risk.

steps.title: Scale
steps.body: Standardize what works and integrate it.

slides.footMessage: Tie next steps to accountable owners and explicit results.
